Die kos wat die nag buite gestaan het
veranderings.voor: is Lerato eerste in die kombuis
veranderings.na: is Lerato die eerste in die kombuis
veranderings.rede: Afrikaans says 'die eerste' for being first to arrive; without the article it reads like an English calque.

veranderings.blok: Die kos wat die nag buite gestaan het
veranderings.rede: These are the party's particular chairs, so the article reads more naturally.

veranderings.blok: Die kos wat die nag buite gestaan het
veranderings.voor: Dit was baie hoender en baie ure se werk.
veranderings.na: Daar is baie hoender in, en dit was baie ure se werk.
veranderings.rede: 'Dit was baie hoender' is wooden and slips out of the present-tense narration; the split keeps both ideas and adds the AWS comma between two clauses.

vlae.blok: Die kos wat die nag buite gestaan het
vlae.teks: Hierdie kos het van gistermiddag af en die hele nag hier buite gestaan.
vlae.rede: A protected entry withdrew 'buite staan' from the rule because a learner read it as meaning a kitchen counter is fine. Here 'buite' describes the story's real stoep, not the rule, and it comes right after the rule sentence that correctly says 'uit die yskas staan'. Probably intended, but a person may want to confirm it cannot be read as the rule. Not changed.
